verdict.rationale: Render ships a first-party MCP server, official plugins, and more than 20 agent skills, so users can manage infrastructure, trigger deploys, and change service plans by talking to AI apps such as Claude Code, Cursor, and Codex. The natural-language layer itself comes from those third-party AI clients rather than from a native conversational interface in Render. missing for 10: a native natural-language command interface in the Render dashboard or CLI, documented coverage of which operations are reachable through natural language, and independent or hands-on corroboration that agent-driven operation works reliably.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can operate the product with natural-language commands

citations.quote: Render's Model Context Protocol (MCP) server enables you to manage your Render infrastructure directly from compatible AI apps, such as Claude Code, Claude Desktop, Codex Desktop, Codex CLI, and Cursor
The Render MCP server now includes a `trigger_deploy` tool that enables you (and your agents) to kick off a new deploy of an existing service.
An agent can inspect CPU and memory metrics, recommend a different compute plan, and apply the change after you approve it.

Render now offers more than 20 official skills for Claude Code, Cursor, and Codex. They give coding agents Render-specific guidance for deploying, configuring, debugging, monitoring, and scaling your applications.
Official Render plugins for Claude Code, Codex, and Cursor configure this server with OAuth automatically.
